newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind to pay US$600 mln for roads.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind to pay US$600 mln for roads.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it would buy a 35 percent stake in two roads in Shanghai for US$600 million, which would be financed by the issue of 139.47 million new shares at HK$34.18 per share.

Its parent Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd (SIIC) agreed to subscribe to the new shares and has placed 48.68 million existing shares with private investors at HK$34.18 per share, the company said in a statement on Thursday.
After the transactions, SIIC's stake in Shanghai Industrial would be maintained at 65.1 percent, the company said.
The placement and susbscription price represent a discount of about 3.7 percent to Wednesday's closing price for Shanghai Industrial shares of HK$35.50.

Shanghai Industrial said the gross proceeds of HK$4.77 billion raised from the new issue would help finance the acquisition of the 35 percent stake in Shanghai's Inner Ring Road and North-to-South Elevated Expressway.

Under the agreement Shanghai City Construction Investment Development General Corp and Shanghai Industrial would form a joint venture to operate, manage and maintain the two roads for 20 years to 2017, it said.

Shanghai City Construction, controlled by the Shanghai municipal government, would guarantee to pay US$25.48 million as after tax distributable income to the joint venture per quarter as "basic income".

The Chinese partner would also pay an "additional income" to the joint venture which would represent 31.25 percent of the annual increase in revenues from tolls, towing and cleaning charges collected from the roads.
Shanghai Industrial said it would receive 80 percent of the net income of the joint venture.

The Inner Ring Road is a 47.66 km two lane expressway surrounding Shanghai City and the North-to-South Elevated Expressway is a 78.45 km principal expressway of three lanes located in the centre of the city.
After the acquisition, Shanghai Industrial said it would have investments in the entire elevated roadway system in Shanghai.
